sections.title_en: Past simple: irregular verbs and questions
sections.title_ru: Past Simple: неправильные глаголы и вопросы
sections.summary_en: Irregular verbs have special past forms (go – went, see – saw). Negatives and questions use did + base verb.
sections.summary_ru: У неправильных глаголов особые формы прошедшего времени (go – went, see – saw). Отрицания и вопросы строятся с did + начальная форма.

rules.body_en: Regular verbs add -ed in the past (work – worked). Irregular verbs change in a different way, and you have to learn each form: go – went, see – saw, have – had, buy – bought. There is no rule, so the best way is to learn them in groups and use them often.
rules.body_ru: Правильные глаголы в прошедшем времени получают окончание -ed (work – worked). Неправильные меняются по-своему, и их формы нужно просто выучить: go – went, see – saw, have – had, buy – bought. Правила нет, поэтому учите их группами и чаще используйте в речи. Заметьте: в русском прошедшее время образуется легко (шёл, видел), а в английском форму нужно помнить.

examples.en: I went to the shop and bought some milk.
examples.ru: Я пошёл в магазин и купил молока.

examples.en: She saw her friend at the station.
We had a great time in Spain.
examples.ru: Мы отлично провели время в Испании.

rules.body_en: Learn these first: be – was/were, go – went, come – came, have – had, make – made, take – took, get – got, give – gave, say – said, see – saw, eat – ate, drink – drank, write – wrote, read – read, think – thought, know – knew, put – put. Some verbs do not change at all: put – put, cut – cut, read – read (but the past is pronounced 'red').
rules.body_ru: Сначала выучите эти: be – was/were, go – went, come – came, have – had, make – made, take – took, get – got, give – gave, say – said, see – saw, eat – ate, drink – drank, write – wrote, read – read, think – thought, know – knew, put – put. Некоторые глаголы вообще не меняются: put – put, cut – cut, read – read (но в прошедшем времени read читается как «ред»).

examples.en: He made dinner and we ate together.
examples.ru: Он приготовил ужин, и мы поели вместе.

examples.en: I read a good book last week.
examples.ru: На прошлой неделе я прочитал хорошую книгу.

examples.en: They took a taxi to the airport.

rules.body_en: In the past simple the verb has the same form for I, you, he, she, it, we and they: I went, she went, they went. The only exception is 'be': I/he/she/it was, you/we/they were. This is easier than the present, where he/she/it adds -s.
rules.body_ru: В Past Simple глагол одинаков для всех лиц: I went, she went, they went. Единственное исключение – глагол be: I/he/she/it was, you/we/they were. В русском форма зависит от рода и числа (он пошёл, она пошла, они пошли), а в английском всегда одна – went.

examples.en: She came home at six, and they came at seven.
examples.ru: Она пришла домой в шесть, а они пришли в семь.

examples.en: I was tired, and my friends were tired too.
examples.ru: Я устал, и мои друзья тоже устали.

rules.body_en: To make a negative, use did not (didn't) and the base form of the verb: I didn't go, she didn't see, they didn't have. Do not use the past form after didn't: 'I didn't went' is wrong. With 'be' there is no didn't: I wasn't, they weren't.
rules.body_ru: Для отрицания используйте did not (didn't) и начальную форму глагола: I didn't go, she didn't see, they didn't have. После didn't нельзя ставить прошедшую форму: «I didn't went» – ошибка, прошедшее время уже выражено словом did. С глаголом be didn't не нужен: I wasn't, they weren't.

examples.en: I didn't see the message yesterday.
We didn't go out because it was cold.
examples.ru: Мы не пошли гулять, потому что было холодно.

examples.en: He wasn't at work on Monday.
examples.ru: В понедельник его не было на работе.

rules.body_en: Questions start with Did + subject + base verb: Did you go? Did she call? The main verb stays in the base form. Short answers: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't. For 'be', put was/were first: Was it good? Were you there?
rules.body_ru: Вопрос начинается с Did + подлежащее + начальная форма: Did you go? Did she call? Главный глагол не меняется. Краткие ответы: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't. В русском вопрос делается интонацией («Ты ходил?»), а в английском нужно вспомогательное did в начале. С глаголом be ставим was/were вперёд: Was it good? Were you there?

examples.en: Did you have a good weekend? – Yes, I did.
examples.ru: У тебя были хорошие выходные? – Да.

examples.en: Did they win the game? – No, they didn't.
Was the film long? – Yes, it was.

rules.title_ru: Специальные вопросы и вопросы к подлежащему
rules.body_en: Put the question word before did: Where did you go? What did she say? When did they arrive? But when the question word is the subject (who or what did the action), do not use did: Who called you? What happened? Here the verb is in the past form.
rules.body_ru: Вопросительное слово ставится перед did: Where did you go? What did she say? When did they arrive? Но если вопрос задаётся к подлежащему (кто или что сделал действие), did не нужен: Who called you? What happened? Здесь глагол стоит в прошедшей форме, как в русском «Кто позвонил?».

examples.en: Where did you buy this jacket?
What time did the train leave?
Who told you about the party?

rules.body_en: The past simple often goes with a finished time: yesterday, last night, last week, two days ago, in 2015, when I was a child. 'Ago' comes after the time: three years ago. These words tell you that the action is finished.
rules.body_ru: Past Simple обычно сопровождают указания на законченное время: yesterday, last night, last week, two days ago, in 2015, when I was a child. Слово ago стоит после периода: three years ago – «три года назад». Важно: в английском одно время Past Simple передаёт и русское «читал», и «прочитал» – вид глагола не важен.

examples.en: I started this job two months ago.
examples.ru: Я начал эту работу два месяца назад.

examples.en: We met in 2015.
Last night I wrote three emails.
examples.ru: Вчера вечером я написал три письма.

exercises.q: Yesterday I ___ to the cinema.
exercises.explain_en: 'Go' is irregular: the past form is 'went'.
exercises.explain_ru: Go – неправильный глагол, его прошедшая форма – went.

exercises.q: She ___ a new phone last week.
exercises.explain_en: 'Buy' is irregular: buy – bought.
exercises.explain_ru: Buy – неправильный глагол: buy – bought.

exercises.q: ___ you see the film?
exercises.explain_en: Past questions start with 'did' and use the base verb.
exercises.explain_ru: Вопрос в прошедшем времени начинается с did, глагол – в начальной форме.

exercises.q: We didn't ___ breakfast this morning.
exercises.explain_en: After 'didn't' use the base form: didn't have.
exercises.explain_ru: После didn't ставим начальную форму: didn't have.

exercises.q: Where ___ they go on holiday?
exercises.explain_en: The question word comes first, then 'did': Where did they go?
exercises.explain_ru: Сначала вопросительное слово, потом did: Where did they go?

exercises.q: He ___ me a letter two days ago.
exercises.explain_en: 'Write' is irregular: write – wrote. 'Ago' shows finished past time.
exercises.explain_ru: Write – неправильный глагол: write – wrote. Ago указывает на прошедшее время.

exercises.q: Who ___ you at the party?
exercises.explain_en: 'Who' is the subject here, so there is no 'did': Who saw you?
exercises.explain_ru: Who – подлежащее, поэтому did не нужен: Who saw you?

exercises.q: ___ it cold yesterday?
exercises.explain_en: With 'be' we do not use 'did'. 'It' takes 'was'.
exercises.explain_ru: С глаголом be did не используется. С it – was.

exercises.q: I ___ (eat) pizza for dinner last night.
exercises.explain_en: 'Eat' is irregular: eat – ate.
exercises.explain_ru: Eat – неправильный глагол: eat – ate.

exercises.q: They ___ (not / go) to school yesterday.
exercises.explain_en: Negative: didn't + base verb.
exercises.explain_ru: Отрицание: didn't + начальная форма глагола.

exercises.q: ___ (you / drink) coffee this morning?
exercises.explain_en: Question: Did + subject + base verb.
exercises.explain_ru: Вопрос: Did + подлежащее + начальная форма.

exercises.q: She ___ (take) the bus to work.
exercises.explain_en: 'Take' is irregular: take – took.
exercises.explain_ru: Take – неправильный глагол: take – took.

exercises.q: We ___ (come) home late.
exercises.explain_en: 'Come' is irregular: come – came.
exercises.explain_ru: Come – неправильный глагол: come – came.

exercises.q: What time ___ (he / get) up?
exercises.explain_en: After the question word: did + subject + base verb.
exercises.explain_ru: После вопросительного слова: did + подлежащее + начальная форма.

exercises.q: 'I goed to London last year' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: 'Go' is irregular. The correct form is 'went'.
exercises.explain_ru: Go – неправильный глагол. Правильно: went.

exercises.q: In questions with 'did', the main verb is in the base form.
exercises.explain_en: Correct: Did you go? (not 'Did you went?').
exercises.explain_ru: Верно: Did you go? (а не «Did you went?»).

exercises.q: 'She didn't saw the film' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: After 'didn't' use the base form: She didn't see the film.
exercises.explain_ru: После didn't нужна начальная форма: She didn't see the film.

exercises.q: The past form of 'read' is spelled the same as the base form.
exercises.explain_en: Read – read. The spelling is the same, but the past is pronounced 'red'.
exercises.explain_ru: Read – read. Пишется одинаково, но в прошедшем читается «ред».

exercises.q: 'Who called you?' is a correct question.
exercises.explain_en: 'Who' is the subject, so we do not add 'did'.
exercises.explain_ru: Who – подлежащее, поэтому did не добавляем.

exercises.answer: Did you have a good weekend?
We saw a great film last night.
exercises.ru: Вчера вечером мы посмотрели отличный фильм.

exercises.answer: Where did she buy that bag?
He didn't know the answer.

sections.summary_en: Present simple is for habits and facts; present continuous is for actions happening now. State verbs (like, know, want) stay in the simple form.
sections.summary_ru: Present Simple – для привычек и фактов, Present Continuous – для действий, которые происходят сейчас. Глаголы состояния (like, know, want) в Continuous не используются.

rules.body_en: Use the present simple for things that happen regularly or are always true: I work in a bank. She drinks coffee every morning. Water boils at 100 degrees. Remember the -s with he, she and it: he works, she goes, it rains.
rules.body_ru: Present Simple описывает регулярные действия и общие факты: I work in a bank. She drinks coffee every morning. Water boils at 100 degrees. Не забывайте окончание -s с he, she, it: he works, she goes, it rains. В русском здесь тоже настоящее время, но без различия «обычно / сейчас».

examples.en: My father works in a hospital.
We usually have lunch at one o'clock.
The shop opens at nine.

rules.body_en: Use the present continuous for an action that is happening at this moment or around now: I am reading a good book. They are playing football. The form is am/is/are + verb-ing. The action started before now and has not finished yet.
rules.body_ru: Present Continuous описывает действие, которое происходит прямо сейчас или в этот период: I am reading a good book. They are playing football. Форма: am/is/are + глагол с -ing. Действие началось раньше и ещё не закончилось. В русском такой отдельной формы нет: «я читаю» может означать и «сейчас», и «вообще», а в английском это разные времена.

examples.en: Listen! Someone is singing.
I'm learning English this year.
examples.ru: В этом году я учу английский.

examples.en: The children are sleeping now.

rules.body_en: Most verbs just add -ing: work – working, play – playing. If the verb ends in -e, drop the e: make – making, write – writing. If a short verb ends in one vowel + one consonant, double the consonant: sit – sitting, run – running, swim – swimming. Verbs in -ie change to -ying: lie – lying.
rules.body_ru: Обычно просто добавляется -ing: work – working, play – playing. Если глагол заканчивается на -e, эта e убирается: make – making, write – writing. В коротких глаголах с одной гласной и одной согласной на конце согласная удваивается: sit – sitting, run – running, swim – swimming. Глаголы на -ie меняют её на -ying: lie – lying.

examples.en: She is writing an email.
We are sitting in the park.
He is lying on the sofa.

rules.body_en: Some words help you choose the tense. Present simple: always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day, on Mondays. Present continuous: now, right now, at the moment, today, this week, Look!, Listen! When you see these words, you know which form to use.
rules.body_ru: Некоторые слова подсказывают время. Present Simple: always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day, on Mondays. Present Continuous: now, right now, at the moment, today, this week, Look!, Listen! Увидели такое слово – сразу понятно, какую форму выбрать.

examples.en: I usually walk to work, but today I'm taking the bus.
examples.ru: Обычно я хожу на работу пешком, но сегодня еду на автобусе.

examples.en: He never eats meat.
At the moment she is talking to a customer.
examples.ru: В данный момент она разговаривает с клиентом.

rules.body_en: Some verbs describe states, not actions, and we do not normally use them in the continuous form: like, love, hate, want, need, know, understand, believe, remember, mean, have (= own). Say 'I want a coffee', not 'I am wanting'. But 'have' as an action is fine: I'm having lunch.
rules.body_ru: Некоторые глаголы обозначают состояние, а не действие, и обычно не используются в Continuous: like, love, hate, want, need, know, understand, believe, remember, mean, have (= владеть). Говорите I want a coffee, а не «I am wanting». Но have в значении действия – можно: I'm having lunch («я обедаю»).

examples.en: I know the answer.
She doesn't understand this word.
They have two cars.
We're having dinner now.

rules.title_en: Questions and negatives in both tenses
rules.title_ru: Вопросы и отрицания в обоих временах
rules.body_en: Present simple uses do/does: Do you like tea? She doesn't work here. Present continuous uses am/is/are: Are you listening? He isn't working today. Never mix them: 'Do you listening?' is wrong.
rules.body_ru: В Present Simple вопросы и отрицания строятся с do/does: Do you like tea? She doesn't work here. В Present Continuous – с am/is/are: Are you listening? He isn't working today. Не смешивайте их: «Do you listening?» – ошибка.

examples.en: Does he play the guitar? – Yes, he does.
Is he playing now? – No, he isn't.
I don't drink coffee in the evening.

rules.body_en: The present continuous is also used for things that are temporary, not only for this exact second: I'm living with my parents this month. She's working in a café this summer. Compare with the permanent present simple: I live in Moscow. She works in a bank.
rules.body_ru: Present Continuous также описывает временные ситуации, а не только то, что происходит в эту секунду: I'm living with my parents this month. She's working in a café this summer. Сравните с постоянным Present Simple: I live in Moscow. She works in a bank. По-русски в обоих случаях «живу», «работает», поэтому ориентируйтесь на смысл: временно или постоянно.

examples.en: I'm staying at a hotel this week.
examples.ru: На этой неделе я живу в гостинице.

examples.en: He's studying a lot these days.
examples.ru: В последнее время он много занимается.

exercises.q: Look! It ___ .
exercises.explain_en: 'Look!' points to now, so we use the present continuous.
exercises.explain_ru: Look! указывает на момент сейчас – нужен Present Continuous.

exercises.q: She usually ___ to work by bus.
exercises.explain_en: 'Usually' shows a habit: present simple with -s for 'she'.
exercises.explain_ru: Usually – привычка: Present Simple с окончанием -s для she.

exercises.q: I ___ this song. It's great!
exercises.explain_en: 'Love' is a state verb, so no continuous form.
exercises.explain_ru: Love – глагол состояния, Continuous не используется.

exercises.q: ___ they ___ TV at the moment?
exercises.explain_en: 'At the moment' = now: Are they watching?
exercises.explain_ru: At the moment = сейчас: Are they watching?

exercises.q: We ___ in a hotel this week.
exercises.explain_en: 'This week' is a temporary situation: present continuous.
exercises.explain_ru: This week – временная ситуация: Present Continuous.

exercises.q: He ___ understand the question.
exercises.explain_en: 'Understand' is a state verb: present simple with 'doesn't' for 'he'.
exercises.explain_ru: Understand – глагол состояния: Present Simple, для he – doesn't.

exercises.q: What ___ you ___ right now?
exercises.explain_en: 'Right now' = present continuous: What are you doing?
exercises.explain_ru: Right now указывает на Present Continuous: What are you doing?

exercises.q: My sister ___ meat. She's a vegetarian.
exercises.explain_en: A general fact about her: present simple negative with 'doesn't'.
exercises.explain_ru: Общий факт о ней: отрицание в Present Simple с doesn't.

exercises.q: Be quiet! The baby ___ (sleep).
exercises.explain_en: The action is happening now: is sleeping.
exercises.explain_ru: Действие происходит сейчас: is sleeping.

exercises.q: Tom ___ (play) football every Saturday.
exercises.explain_en: 'Every Saturday' = habit: present simple, plays.
exercises.explain_ru: Every Saturday – привычка: Present Simple, plays.

exercises.q: I ___ (not / like) cold weather.
exercises.explain_en: 'Like' is a state verb: present simple negative.
exercises.explain_ru: Like – глагол состояния: отрицание в Present Simple.

exercises.q: ___ (she / work) today?
exercises.explain_en: 'Today' here means a temporary situation: Is she working?
exercises.explain_ru: Today – временная ситуация: Is she working?

exercises.q: They ___ (sit) in the garden now.
exercises.explain_en: Now = present continuous. Double the t: sitting.
exercises.explain_ru: Now = Present Continuous. Удваиваем t: sitting.

exercises.q: He ___ (know) the answer.
exercises.explain_en: 'Know' is a state verb: present simple with -s.
exercises.explain_ru: Know – глагол состояния: Present Simple с -s.

exercises.q: 'I am wanting a new car' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: 'Want' is a state verb: I want a new car.
exercises.explain_ru: Want – глагол состояния: I want a new car.

exercises.q: We use the present continuous for actions happening now.
exercises.explain_en: Yes: I am reading now.
exercises.explain_ru: Верно: I am reading now.

exercises.q: 'She don't like tea' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: With 'she' we use 'doesn't': She doesn't like tea.
exercises.explain_ru: С she нужно doesn't: She doesn't like tea.

exercises.q: 'Make' becomes 'making' in the -ing form.
exercises.explain_en: Verbs ending in -e drop the e: making.
exercises.explain_ru: У глаголов на -e эта буква убирается: making.

exercises.q: 'I'm having lunch' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: 'Have' means 'eat' here, so it is an action and can be continuous.
exercises.explain_ru: Have здесь значит «есть» – это действие, Continuous возможен.

exercises.answer: She is talking on the phone now.
I always get up at seven.
Are you listening to me?
He doesn't work on Sundays.

sections.title_en: Future: going to, will and present continuous
sections.title_ru: Будущее: going to, will и Present Continuous
sections.summary_en: Going to is for plans and predictions with evidence, will is for quick decisions, offers and opinions, and the present continuous is for fixed arrangements.
sections.summary_ru: Going to – для планов и предсказаний по очевидным признакам, will – для спонтанных решений, предложений и мнений, Present Continuous – для договорённостей.

rules.body_en: Use be going to + verb for a plan or intention you decided before now: I'm going to learn Spanish next year. They are going to buy a car. The form is am/is/are + going to + base verb. Negative: I'm not going to; question: Are you going to?
rules.body_ru: Be going to + глагол выражает план или намерение, которое вы решили заранее: I'm going to learn Spanish next year. They are going to buy a car. Форма: am/is/are + going to + начальная форма. Отрицание: I'm not going to, вопрос: Are you going to? По-русски это «собираюсь, планирую».

examples.en: We're going to visit Italy in May.
examples.ru: В мае мы собираемся поехать в Италию.

examples.en: She's going to start a new job.
I'm not going to buy that bag.
examples.ru: Я не собираюсь покупать эту сумку.

rules.title_en: Going to for predictions with evidence
rules.title_ru: Going to для предсказаний по признакам
rules.body_en: When you can see or know that something will happen, use going to: Look at those clouds – it's going to rain. He's driving too fast – he's going to have an accident. There is evidence now for the future event.
rules.body_ru: Когда вы видите или знаете признаки того, что что-то случится, используйте going to: Look at those clouds – it's going to rain. He's driving too fast – he's going to have an accident. Есть очевидная причина уже сейчас.

examples.en: It's 8:55 and the bus is late. We're going to miss the train.
examples.ru: Уже 8:55, а автобус опаздывает. Мы опоздаем на поезд.

examples.en: She's a great student. She's going to pass.

rules.title_en: Will for decisions, offers and promises
rules.title_ru: Will для решений, предложений и обещаний
rules.body_en: Use will when you decide something at the moment of speaking: The phone's ringing – I'll answer it. Also for offers and promises: I'll help you. I'll call you tomorrow. The form is will + base verb for all persons. Short forms: I'll, you'll, she'll; negative: won't.
rules.body_ru: Will используется для решений, принятых в момент речи: The phone's ringing – I'll answer it. А также для предложений помощи и обещаний: I'll help you. I'll call you tomorrow. Форма: will + начальная форма для всех лиц. Краткие формы: I'll, you'll, she'll, отрицание – won't. В русском это просто будущее «отвечу, помогу, позвоню».

examples.en: It's cold. I'll close the window.
Don't worry, I won't be late.
I'll carry your bag for you.

rules.title_en: Will for opinions about the future
rules.body_en: Use will for predictions that come from your opinion, not from evidence: I think it will be a good film. People will live longer in the future. Common phrases: I think ..., I'm sure ..., probably, maybe.
rules.body_ru: Will нужен для предсказаний, основанных на мнении, а не на видимых признаках: I think it will be a good film. People will live longer in the future. Частые выражения: I think ..., I'm sure ..., probably, maybe.

examples.en: I think she'll like the present.
It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

rules.body_en: For a fixed arrangement with other people, often with a time and place, use the present continuous: I'm meeting Anna at six. We're flying to Rome on Monday. It is like something written in your diary. It is very similar to going to, but sounds more fixed.
rules.body_ru: Для твёрдой договорённости, обычно с указанием времени и места, используется Present Continuous: I'm meeting Anna at six. We're flying to Rome on Monday. Это как запись в ежедневнике. Значение близко к going to, но звучит более определённо. В русском здесь тоже часто настоящее: «Я встречаюсь с Анной в шесть».

examples.en: We're having dinner with my parents tonight.
examples.ru: Сегодня вечером мы ужинаем с моими родителями.

examples.en: She's seeing the doctor at ten tomorrow.
examples.ru: Завтра в десять она идёт к врачу.

rules.body_en: Will: Will you come? – Yes, I will. / No, I won't. Going to: Are you going to stay? – Yes, I am. / No, I'm not. Present continuous: Is she coming? – Yes, she is. Put the question word first: What will you do? Where are you going to live?
rules.body_ru: Will: Will you come? – Yes, I will. / No, I won't. Going to: Are you going to stay? – Yes, I am. / No, I'm not. Present Continuous: Is she coming? – Yes, she is. Вопросительное слово ставится в начало: What will you do? Where are you going to live?

examples.en: Will it be expensive? – No, it won't.
What are you going to do this weekend?
examples.ru: Что ты собираешься делать в выходные?

examples.en: Are they coming to the party?

rules.body_en: Future time words: tomorrow, tonight, next week, in two days, soon, in the future. After when, if, before and after we use the present simple, not will: I'll call you when I arrive. If it rains, we'll stay at home.
rules.body_ru: Слова будущего времени: tomorrow, tonight, next week, in two days, soon, in the future. После when, if, before и after используется Present Simple, а не will: I'll call you when I arrive. If it rains, we'll stay at home. Это отличается от русского: «когда я приеду» – будущее, а в английском – настоящее.

examples.en: I'll text you when I get home.

examples.en: If you're tired, we'll go home.
examples.ru: Если ты устал, мы пойдём домой.

examples.en: See you next week!

sections.summary_en: Countable nouns have a plural (two apples); uncountable nouns do not (some water). Use some/any, much/many/a lot of and a few/a little with them.
sections.summary_ru: Исчисляемые существительные имеют множественное число (two apples), неисчисляемые – нет (some water). С ними используются some/any, much/many/a lot of и a few/a little.

rules.body_en: Countable nouns can be counted: one apple, two apples, a car. Uncountable nouns have no plural and no a/an: water, money, bread, music, information, advice, furniture. Say 'some water', not 'a water'. In English the noun decides, not the meaning, so learn which group a word belongs to.
rules.body_ru: Исчисляемые существительные можно посчитать: one apple, two apples, a car. Неисчисляемые не имеют множественного числа и не сочетаются с a/an: water, money, bread, music, information, advice, furniture. Говорите some water, а не «a water». Внимание: в английском неисчисляемы слова, которые в русском считаются: advice (совет – советы), news, information, furniture, hair. Эти слова нужно запомнить.

examples.en: I have two apples and some bread.
examples.ru: У меня два яблока и немного хлеба.

examples.en: Can you give me some advice?
We need new furniture for the flat.
examples.ru: Нам нужна новая мебель для квартиры.

rules.body_en: Use some in positive sentences: I have some friends here. There is some milk. Use any in negatives and questions: I don't have any money. Are there any shops near here? In offers and requests we use some: Would you like some tea? Can I have some water?
rules.body_ru: Some используется в утвердительных предложениях: I have some friends here. There is some milk. Any – в отрицаниях и вопросах: I don't have any money. Are there any shops near here? В предложениях и просьбах ставим some: Would you like some tea? Can I have some water? В русском эти слова часто вообще не переводятся.

examples.en: There are some eggs in the fridge.
We don't have any sugar.
Would you like some coffee?

rules.title_en: Much, many and a lot of
rules.title_ru: Much, many и a lot of
rules.body_en: Many goes with countable plurals: many people, many cars. Much goes with uncountable nouns: much time, much money. Much and many are common in questions and negatives. In positive sentences we usually say a lot of (or lots of), which works with both: a lot of friends, a lot of water.
rules.body_ru: Many сочетается с исчисляемыми во множественном числе: many people, many cars. Much – с неисчисляемыми: much time, much money. Much и many обычны в вопросах и отрицаниях. В утверждениях чаще говорят a lot of (или lots of), и это подходит для обоих типов: a lot of friends, a lot of water. По-русски всё это «много».

examples.en: I don't have much time today.
Are there many students in your class?
She has a lot of books.

rules.body_en: A few means a small number and goes with countable nouns: a few friends, a few minutes. A little means a small amount and goes with uncountable nouns: a little milk, a little time. Both mean 'some, but not much'.
rules.body_ru: A few – «несколько, немного» с исчисляемыми: a few friends, a few minutes. A little – «немного» с неисчисляемыми: a little milk, a little time. Оба значат «есть немного». В русском одно слово «немного», а в английском выбор зависит от существительного.

examples.en: I have a few questions.
There is a little sugar left.
Wait a few minutes, please.

rules.body_en: To ask about quantity, use how many with countable nouns and how much with uncountable nouns: How many brothers do you have? How much water do you drink? How much also asks about price: How much is it? How much does it cost?
rules.body_ru: Чтобы спросить о количестве, используйте how many с исчисляемыми и how much с неисчисляемыми: How many brothers do you have? How much water do you drink? How much также спрашивает о цене: How much is it? How much does it cost? По-русски оба варианта – «сколько».

examples.en: How many people are coming?
How much money do you need?
How much is this jacket?

rules.body_en: To count an uncountable noun, use a container or a unit: a cup of tea, a glass of water, a bottle of milk, a piece of advice, a slice of bread, a bar of chocolate, a kilo of rice. Then you can make it plural: two cups of coffee.
rules.body_ru: Чтобы посчитать неисчисляемое, добавьте ёмкость или единицу: a cup of tea, a glass of water, a bottle of milk, a piece of advice, a slice of bread, a bar of chocolate, a kilo of rice. Тогда появляется множественное число: two cups of coffee. Так же по-русски: «два совета» будет two pieces of advice.

examples.en: Two coffees, please. – Two cups of coffee.
examples.ru: Два кофе, пожалуйста. – Две чашки кофе.

examples.en: He gave me a piece of good advice.

rules.title_en: Uncountable nouns take a singular verb
rules.title_ru: Неисчисляемые – с глаголом в единственном числе
rules.body_en: Uncountable nouns use a singular verb and 'it': The news is good. Money isn't everything. This information is useful. Be careful with words that are plural in Russian but uncountable in English: news, hair, money, furniture.
rules.body_ru: Неисчисляемые существительные сочетаются с глаголом в единственном числе и местоимением it: The news is good. Money isn't everything. This information is useful. Особенно следите за словами, которые в русском стоят во множественном числе: «новости» – news is, «деньги» – money is, «волосы» – hair is, «мебель» – furniture is.

examples.en: The news is on at nine.
Her hair is very long.

sections.summary_en: Short adjectives add -er/-est, long adjectives use more/most, and some are irregular (good – better – best). Use than after a comparative and as ... as for equal things.
sections.summary_ru: Короткие прилагательные получают -er/-est, длинные – more/most, а некоторые образуют степени неправильно (good – better – best). После сравнительной степени ставится than, для равенства – as ... as.

rules.body_en: One-syllable adjectives add -er for the comparative and -est for the superlative: tall – taller – the tallest, old – older – the oldest. The superlative almost always has 'the' before it. Use the comparative for two things and the superlative for three or more.
rules.body_ru: Односложные прилагательные получают -er в сравнительной степени и -est в превосходной: tall – taller – the tallest, old – older – the oldest. Перед превосходной степенью почти всегда стоит the. Сравнительная степень – для двух предметов, превосходная – для трёх и более. Русское «самый» = the + -est.

examples.en: My brother is older than me.
This is the oldest building in the town.
examples.ru: Это самое старое здание в городе.

examples.en: Today is colder than yesterday.

rules.body_en: If the adjective ends in -e, add only -r/-st: nice – nicer – nicest, large – larger – largest. Short adjectives with one vowel + one consonant double the consonant: big – bigger – biggest, hot – hotter – hottest. If it ends in -y, change y to i: happy – happier – happiest, easy – easier – easiest.
rules.body_ru: Если прилагательное заканчивается на -e, добавляется только -r/-st: nice – nicer – nicest, large – larger – largest. В коротких словах с одной гласной и одной согласной на конце согласная удваивается: big – bigger – biggest, hot – hotter – hottest. Если слово заканчивается на -y, она меняется на i: happy – happier – happiest, easy – easier – easiest.

examples.en: This room is bigger than mine.
She is the happiest person I know.
examples.ru: Она самый счастливый человек из тех, кого я знаю.

examples.en: The test was easier than I thought.
examples.ru: Тест оказался легче, чем я думал.

rules.body_en: Adjectives with two or more syllables usually use more and the most: expensive – more expensive – the most expensive, beautiful – more beautiful – the most beautiful. Never use both: 'more bigger' is wrong. Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y take -er/-est (easier, funnier).
rules.body_ru: Прилагательные из двух и более слогов обычно образуют степени с more и the most: expensive – more expensive – the most expensive, beautiful – more beautiful – the most beautiful. Нельзя использовать оба способа сразу: «more bigger» – ошибка. Двусложные на -y получают -er/-est (easier, funnier). В русском «более» можно добавить почти к любому слову, а в английском выбор зависит от длины.

examples.en: A car is more expensive than a bike.
This is the most interesting book I have.
examples.ru: Это самая интересная книга из всех, что у меня есть.

examples.en: English is more difficult than I thought.

rules.body_en: Some adjectives have special forms that you must learn: good – better – the best, bad – worse – the worst, far – further – the furthest (also farther – farthest), little – less – the least, much/many – more – the most.
rules.body_ru: У некоторых прилагательных особые формы, их нужно выучить: good – better – the best, bad – worse – the worst, far – further – the furthest (также farther – farthest), little – less – the least, much/many – more – the most. Сравните с русским: хороший – лучше – лучший, плохой – хуже – худший.

examples.en: Her English is better than mine.
It was the worst day of my life.
examples.ru: Это был худший день в моей жизни.

examples.en: The station is further than the bank.

rules.body_en: After a comparative we use than: taller than me, more expensive than this one. After a superlative we often say in + place or group (the best restaurant in town, the tallest in the class) or of + period (the happiest day of my life).
rules.body_ru: После сравнительной степени ставится than («чем»): taller than me, more expensive than this one. После превосходной степени обычно идёт in + место или группа (the best restaurant in town, the tallest in the class) или of + период (the happiest day of my life). Обратите внимание: по-русски «самый высокий в классе», а по-английски in the class, не «of the class».

examples.en: Moscow is bigger than St Petersburg.
He is the best player in the team.
It was the coldest night of the year.
examples.ru: Это была самая холодная ночь в году.

rules.body_en: To say that two things are the same, use as + adjective + as: She is as tall as her mother. The negative not as ... as means 'less': This film isn't as good as the book. Do not use a comparative here: 'as taller as' is wrong.
rules.body_ru: Чтобы сказать, что два предмета одинаковы, используйте as + прилагательное + as: She is as tall as her mother («такая же высокая, как»). Отрицание not as ... as значит «менее»: This film isn't as good as the book. Сравнительная степень здесь не нужна: «as taller as» – ошибка.

examples.en: My bag is as heavy as yours.
examples.ru: Моя сумка такая же тяжёлая, как твоя.

examples.en: This hotel isn't as expensive as the other one.
examples.ru: Этот отель не такой дорогой, как другой.

rules.title_en: Much, a lot and a bit with comparatives
rules.title_ru: Much, a lot и a bit со сравнительной степенью
rules.body_en: To make a comparison stronger, use much or a lot before the comparative: much better, a lot more expensive. For a small difference use a bit or a little: a bit cheaper, a little older. Do not use 'very' with a comparative: 'very better' is wrong.
rules.body_ru: Чтобы усилить сравнение, поставьте much или a lot перед сравнительной степенью: much better («намного лучше»), a lot more expensive. Для небольшой разницы – a bit или a little: a bit cheaper, a little older. Very со сравнительной степенью не используется: «very better» – ошибка.

examples.en: This car is much faster than the old one.
The new flat is a bit smaller.
Trains are a lot more comfortable than buses.

exercises.explain_en: 'Tall' is short: add -er. 'Than' follows the comparative.
exercises.explain_ru: Tall – короткое прилагательное: добавляем -er. После него – than.

exercises.explain_en: 'Interesting' is long: the most interesting.
exercises.explain_ru: Interesting – длинное слово: the most interesting.

exercises.explain_en: Short adjective with one vowel + one consonant: double the t.
exercises.explain_ru: Короткое слово с одной гласной и согласной на конце: удваиваем t.

sections.title_en: Modals: must, have to, should, may/might
sections.title_ru: Модальные глаголы: must, have to, should, may/might
sections.summary_en: Must and have to express obligation, mustn't means it is not allowed, should gives advice, and may/might show possibility.
sections.summary_ru: Must и have to выражают обязанность, mustn't – запрет, should – совет, may/might – возможность.

rules.body_en: Modal verbs (must, should, may, might) are followed by the base verb without 'to': You must go, she should rest. They have no -s with he/she/it and no -ing form. Questions are made by putting the modal first: Should I call him? Negatives add not: must not (mustn't), should not (shouldn't).
rules.body_ru: После модальных глаголов (must, should, may, might) идёт начальная форма без to: You must go, she should rest. У них нет -s в третьем лице и формы на -ing. Вопрос образуется перестановкой: Should I call him? Отрицание – добавляем not: must not (mustn't), should not (shouldn't). Вспомогательный do здесь не нужен.

examples.en: She must be at work by nine.
examples.ru: Она должна быть на работе к девяти.

examples.en: Should we take a taxi?
You shouldn't eat so much sugar.
examples.ru: Тебе не стоит есть так много сахара.

rules.body_en: Must means it is very important or necessary. It often shows the speaker's own opinion or a rule: I must call my mother. You must wear a seatbelt. Must has only one form for all persons and no past form.
rules.body_ru: Must значит «обязательно нужно». Часто это мнение говорящего или правило: I must call my mother. You must wear a seatbelt. Форма одна для всех лиц, прошедшего времени у must нет. Русское «должен» переводится и как must, и как have to.

examples.en: I must finish this today.
You must show your ticket.
We must hurry, the train leaves at ten.
examples.ru: Нам надо спешить, поезд уходит в десять.

rules.title_ru: Have to: обязанность по внешним причинам
rules.body_en: Have to also means 'it is necessary', but usually because of a rule, a job or a situation, not the speaker's opinion: I have to work on Saturdays. Have to is not a modal: it changes to has to with he/she/it and uses do/does in questions and negatives: Do you have to go? He doesn't have to pay.
rules.body_ru: Have to тоже значит «нужно», но обычно из-за правил, работы или обстоятельств, а не по желанию говорящего: I have to work on Saturdays. Have to – не модальный глагол: с he/she/it он становится has to, а вопросы и отрицания строятся с do/does: Do you have to go? He doesn't have to pay. По-русски это часто «приходится, нужно».

examples.en: She has to wear a uniform at work.
examples.ru: На работе ей приходится носить форму.

examples.en: Do you have to get up early tomorrow?
We have to be at the airport at six.
examples.ru: Нам нужно быть в аэропорту в шесть.

rules.body_en: These are very different. Mustn't means it is not allowed: You mustn't smoke here. Don't have to means it is not necessary, you can choose: You don't have to come if you are busy. Compare: You mustn't pay (it's forbidden) and You don't have to pay (it's free).
rules.body_ru: Это совершенно разные значения. Mustn't – «нельзя, запрещено»: You mustn't smoke here. Don't have to – «не обязательно, можно не делать»: You don't have to come if you are busy. Сравните: You mustn't pay (платить запрещено) и You don't have to pay (платить не нужно, это бесплатно). Русское «не должен» может значить и то, и другое, поэтому будьте внимательны.

examples.en: You mustn't touch this. It's dangerous.
You don't have to wash the dishes. I'll do it.
examples.ru: Тебе не нужно мыть посуду. Я сам.

examples.en: Students mustn't use phones in the exam.
examples.ru: Студентам нельзя пользоваться телефонами на экзамене.

rules.body_en: Use should to say that something is a good idea, and shouldn't when it is a bad idea: You should see a doctor. You shouldn't drive so fast. To ask for advice, say Should I ...? Should is softer than must.
rules.body_ru: Should говорит, что что-то – хорошая идея, а shouldn't – плохая: You should see a doctor. You shouldn't drive so fast. Чтобы попросить совета, скажите Should I ...? Should мягче, чем must. По-русски – «следует, стоит, надо бы».

examples.en: You should drink more water.
Should I buy the blue one or the red one?
He shouldn't work so late.
examples.ru: Ему не стоит работать так допоздна.

rules.body_en: May and might mean 'perhaps' or 'it is possible': It might rain later. She may be at home. Might is a little less sure than may, but at this level they are nearly the same. May is also used for polite permission: May I come in? May I ask a question?
rules.body_ru: May и might значат «возможно, может быть»: It might rain later. She may be at home. Might звучит чуть менее уверенно, чем may, но на этом уровне разница почти не важна. May также используется для вежливого разрешения: May I come in? May I ask a question? Отрицание: may not, might not (без сокращения mightn't в речи почти нет).

examples.en: I might be late tonight.
Take an umbrella. It may rain.
May I use your phone?

rules.body_en: Must has no past form. To talk about obligation in the past, use had to: Yesterday I had to work late. Negative: didn't have to; question: Did you have to ...? Should and might do not change in simple past stories at this level, so use had to for 'was necessary'.
rules.body_ru: У must нет прошедшего времени. Чтобы сказать об обязанности в прошлом, используйте had to: Yesterday I had to work late («мне пришлось»). Отрицание: didn't have to, вопрос: Did you have to ...? Запомните: «я должен был» = I had to, а не «I musted».

examples.en: We had to wait for an hour.
Did you have to pay for the ticket?
She didn't have to go to school yesterday.
examples.ru: Вчера ей не нужно было идти в школу.

exercises.q: You ___ wear a seatbelt in the car. It's the law.
exercises.explain_en: A rule or law: must.
exercises.explain_ru: Правило или закон: must.

exercises.q: I ___ work tomorrow. It's Sunday.
exercises.explain_en: It is not necessary: don't have to.
exercises.explain_ru: Нет необходимости: don't have to.

exercises.q: You ___ smoke here. It's not allowed.
exercises.explain_en: It is forbidden: mustn't.
exercises.explain_ru: Запрещено: mustn't.

exercises.q: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early.
exercises.explain_en: Advice: should.
exercises.explain_ru: Совет: should.

exercises.q: It ___ rain later. Take an umbrella.
exercises.explain_en: Possibility: might (= maybe).
exercises.explain_ru: Возможность: might (= может быть).

exercises.q: She ___ to get up at six every day for work.
exercises.explain_en: 'Have to' changes to 'has to' with she. Modals never take 'to'.
exercises.explain_ru: Have to с she превращается в has to. Модальные глаголы с to не сочетаются.

exercises.q: ___ I open the window?
exercises.explain_en: Asking for permission: May I ...?
exercises.explain_ru: Просьба о разрешении: May I ...?

exercises.q: ___ you have to work on Saturdays?
exercises.explain_en: 'Have to' makes questions with do/does.
exercises.explain_ru: Вопросы с have to строятся через do/does.

exercises.q: You ___ (must / not) be late for the exam.
exercises.explain_en: Not allowed: mustn't.
exercises.explain_ru: Запрет: mustn't.

exercises.q: He ___ (have to) wear a uniform at work.
exercises.explain_en: With he: has to.
exercises.explain_ru: С he: has to.

exercises.q: I think you ___ (should / not) eat so much chocolate.
exercises.explain_en: Advice not to do something: shouldn't.
exercises.explain_ru: Совет не делать: shouldn't.

exercises.q: We ___ (not / have to) pay. It's free.
exercises.explain_en: Not necessary: don't have to.
exercises.explain_ru: Нет необходимости: don't have to.

exercises.q: Take a coat. It ___ (may) be cold tonight.
exercises.explain_en: Possibility: may / might + base verb.
exercises.explain_ru: Возможность: may / might + начальная форма.

exercises.q: Yesterday I ___ (have to) work late.
exercises.explain_en: Past obligation: had to.
exercises.explain_ru: Обязанность в прошлом: had to.

exercises.q: 'You mustn't' and 'you don't have to' mean the same.
exercises.explain_en: Mustn't = not allowed; don't have to = not necessary.
exercises.explain_ru: Mustn't – нельзя; don't have to – не обязательно.

exercises.q: After 'must' we use the base verb without 'to'.
exercises.explain_en: Yes: You must go (not 'must to go').
exercises.explain_ru: Верно: You must go (а не «must to go»).

exercises.q: 'She must to go now' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: No 'to' after must: She must go now.
exercises.explain_ru: После must нет to: She must go now.

exercises.q: 'Might' means something is possible but not certain.
exercises.explain_en: Yes: It might rain = maybe it will rain.
exercises.explain_ru: Верно: It might rain = возможно, пойдёт дождь.

exercises.q: 'He have to go' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: With he/she/it: has to.
exercises.explain_ru: С he/she/it: has to.

exercises.answer: You should drink more water.
Do we have to finish today?
I might be late tonight.
You mustn't use your phone here.

sections.summary_en: Present perfect (have/has + past participle) talks about life experience and recent events with a result now. Key words: ever, never, just, already, yet; been vs gone.
sections.summary_ru: Present Perfect (have/has + третья форма) описывает жизненный опыт и недавние события с результатом сейчас. Ключевые слова: ever, never, just, already, yet; been и gone.

rules.body_en: The present perfect is have/has + the past participle. For regular verbs the participle is the -ed form: worked, played. Irregular verbs have a third form you must learn: go – went – gone, see – saw – seen, eat – ate – eaten, write – wrote – written. Short forms: I've, you've, he's, she's, we've, they've.
rules.body_ru: Present Perfect образуется как have/has + причастие прошедшего времени (третья форма). У правильных глаголов это форма на -ed: worked, played. У неправильных – особая третья форма, которую нужно выучить: go – went – gone, see – saw – seen, eat – ate – eaten, write – wrote – written. Сокращения: I've, you've, he's, she's, we've, they've. В русском такого времени нет – переводится обычным прошедшим.

examples.en: I have worked here for two years.
She has written three books.
We've eaten all the cake.

rules.body_en: Use the present perfect to talk about experiences in your life up to now, without saying when: I have been to Italy. Ever is used in questions ('at any time in your life'): Have you ever eaten sushi? Never means 'at no time': I have never seen snow.
rules.body_ru: Present Perfect описывает опыт за всю жизнь до настоящего момента, без указания когда: I have been to Italy. Ever используется в вопросах («когда-нибудь»): Have you ever eaten sushi? Never значит «никогда»: I have never seen snow. Заметьте: с never не нужно второе отрицание, в отличие от русского «никогда не видел».

examples.en: Have you ever been to London?
I've never tried Indian food.
examples.ru: Я никогда не пробовал индийскую еду.

examples.en: He has visited many countries.

rules.title_en: Recent events with a result now
rules.body_en: Use the present perfect for a past action that is important now: I've lost my keys (so I can't open the door). She has broken her leg (so she can't walk). We do not say when it happened; the result is what matters.
rules.body_ru: Present Perfect описывает действие в прошлом, результат которого важен сейчас: I've lost my keys (поэтому не могу открыть дверь). She has broken her leg (поэтому не может ходить). Когда именно это случилось, не говорится – важен результат. В русском здесь обычно глагол совершенного вида: потерял, сломала.

examples.en: I've lost my phone. Can you call it?
examples.ru: Я потерял телефон. Можешь позвонить на него?

examples.en: The shop has closed. We're too late.
Tom has bought a new car.

rules.body_en: Just = a short time ago; already = before now, maybe earlier than expected. Both go between have and the participle: I've just eaten. She has already left. Yet means 'until now' and goes at the end of negatives and questions: I haven't finished yet. Have you finished yet?
rules.body_ru: Just – «только что», already – «уже», часто раньше, чем ожидалось. Оба стоят между have и причастием: I've just eaten. She has already left. Yet значит «ещё / уже» в отрицаниях и вопросах и ставится в конец: I haven't finished yet («ещё не закончил»). Have you finished yet? («уже закончил?»).

examples.en: We've just arrived at the hotel.
examples.ru: Мы только что приехали в отель.

examples.en: I've already seen this film.
Has he called yet? – No, not yet.
examples.ru: Он уже звонил? – Нет, ещё нет.

rules.body_en: Has been to means the person went somewhere and came back: She has been to Paris (she is here now). Has gone to means the person went and is still there: She has gone to Paris (she is in Paris now). Use been for experience and gone for 'not here'.
rules.body_ru: Has been to значит, что человек съездил и вернулся: She has been to Paris (она сейчас здесь). Has gone to – уехал и всё ещё там: She has gone to Paris (она сейчас в Париже). Для опыта используйте been, для «его сейчас нет» – gone. По-русски «была в Париже» и «уехала в Париж».

examples.en: I've been to Rome twice.
Where's Anna? – She's gone to the shop.
examples.ru: Где Анна? – Она ушла в магазин.

examples.en: Have you ever been to a concert?

rules.body_en: If you say when something happened (yesterday, last week, in 2010, two days ago), use the past simple: I saw him yesterday. If the time is not important or not finished (ever, never, just, already, yet, today, this week), use the present perfect: I have seen him today. Never say 'I have seen him yesterday'.
rules.body_ru: Если указано, когда это произошло (yesterday, last week, in 2010, two days ago), нужен Past Simple: I saw him yesterday. Если время не важно или ещё не закончилось (ever, never, just, already, yet, today, this week), нужен Present Perfect: I have seen him today. Нельзя сказать «I have seen him yesterday». В русском оба варианта – просто прошедшее время, поэтому ориентируйтесь на слова-маркеры.

examples.en: I went to Spain in 2019.
examples.ru: Я ездил в Испанию в 2019 году.

examples.en: I have been to Spain three times.
examples.ru: Я был в Испании три раза.

examples.en: She called me an hour ago.

rules.body_en: Put have/has before the subject: Have you finished? Has she arrived? Short answers: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't. / Yes, she has. / No, she hasn't. Question words go first: What have you done? Where has he gone? Remember that 's can mean 'is' or 'has': He's gone = He has gone.
rules.body_ru: Have/has ставится перед подлежащим: Have you finished? Has she arrived? Краткие ответы: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't. / Yes, she has. / No, she hasn't. Вопросительное слово – в начало: What have you done? Where has he gone? Помните, что 's может быть и is, и has: He's gone = He has gone.

examples.en: Have you done your homework? – Yes, I have.
Has it stopped raining? – No, it hasn't.
What have you bought?

exercises.q: I ___ never ___ to Japan.
exercises.explain_en: Life experience: have + been (participle of be/go).
exercises.explain_ru: Жизненный опыт: have + been (третья форма be/go).

exercises.q: ___ you ever ___ sushi?
exercises.explain_en: 'Ever' goes with the present perfect: Have you ever eaten?
exercises.explain_ru: Ever сочетается с Present Perfect: Have you ever eaten?

exercises.q: She has ___ finished her homework. She can go out now.
exercises.explain_en: Just = a short time ago, between has and the participle.
exercises.explain_ru: Just = только что, между has и причастием.

exercises.q: Have you done your homework ___ ?
exercises.explain_en: 'Yet' goes at the end of questions.
exercises.explain_ru: Yet ставится в конец вопроса.

exercises.q: Tom isn't here. He ___ to the shop.
exercises.explain_en: He is still there: has gone.
exercises.explain_ru: Он всё ещё там: has gone.

exercises.q: I ___ my keys. I can't open the door.
exercises.explain_en: A result now: have + lost (participle).
exercises.explain_ru: Результат сейчас: have + lost (третья форма).

exercises.q: We ___ to Paris last year.
exercises.explain_en: 'Last year' is a finished time: past simple.
exercises.explain_ru: Last year – законченное время: Past Simple.

exercises.q: ___ she ___ the new film?
exercises.explain_en: With she: has + seen.
exercises.explain_ru: С she: has + seen.

exercises.q: I ___ (see) this film three times.
exercises.explain_en: Experience up to now: have seen.
exercises.explain_ru: Опыт до настоящего момента: have seen.

exercises.q: She ___ (not / finish) the book yet.
exercises.explain_en: Negative with she: hasn't finished.
exercises.explain_ru: Отрицание с she: hasn't finished.

exercises.q: ___ (you / ever / be) to Italy?
exercises.explain_en: Have + subject + ever + been.
exercises.explain_ru: Have + подлежащее + ever + been.

exercises.q: They ___ (just / arrive).
exercises.explain_en: Just goes between have and the participle.
exercises.explain_ru: Just стоит между have и причастием.

exercises.q: He ___ (already / eat) lunch.
exercises.explain_en: Has + already + eaten.
exercises.explain_ru: Порядок: has + already + eaten.

exercises.q: I ___ (never / try) Indian food.
exercises.explain_en: Have + never + tried. No extra 'not'.
exercises.explain_ru: Have + never + tried. Второе отрицание не нужно.

exercises.q: 'I have went to London' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: Use the participle: I have gone / I have been to London.
exercises.explain_ru: Нужна третья форма: I have gone / I have been to London.

exercises.q: 'Yet' usually comes at the end of a negative sentence or question.
exercises.explain_en: Yes: I haven't finished yet. Have you finished yet?
exercises.explain_ru: Верно: I haven't finished yet. Have you finished yet?

exercises.q: 'She has been to Paris' means she is in Paris now.
exercises.explain_en: 'Has been' means she went and came back. 'Has gone' = she is there now.
exercises.explain_ru: Has been – съездила и вернулась. Has gone – она сейчас там.

exercises.q: We use 'ever' mainly in questions.
exercises.explain_en: Yes: Have you ever ...? In negatives we use 'never'.
exercises.explain_ru: Верно: Have you ever ...? В отрицаниях – never.

exercises.q: 'I have seen him yesterday' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: 'Yesterday' needs the past simple: I saw him yesterday.
exercises.explain_ru: С yesterday нужен Past Simple: I saw him yesterday.

exercises.answer: Have you ever been to London?
I've just finished my work.
She hasn't called me yet.
We have already seen this film.
