sections.summary_en: Adjectives describe nouns (a slow car); adverbs describe verbs (he drives slowly). Learn -ly spelling, irregular adverbs like well and fast, too/enough and word order.
sections.summary_ru: Прилагательные описывают существительные (a slow car), наречия – глаголы (he drives slowly). Разберём написание -ly, особые наречия well и fast, too/enough и порядок слов.

rules.body_en: An adjective tells you what a person or thing is like. It goes before the noun (a slow car, a beautiful day) or after be, look, feel, seem: The car is slow. You look tired. English adjectives never change: one big car, two big cars.
rules.body_ru: Прилагательное описывает, какой человек или предмет. Оно стоит перед существительным (a slow car, a beautiful day) или после be, look, feel, seem: The car is slow. You look tired. В отличие от русского, английские прилагательные не меняются по числу и роду: one big car, two big cars – никаких «bigs».

examples.en: She has a small flat in the centre.
examples.ru: У неё маленькая квартира в центре.

examples.en: These shoes are very comfortable.
He looks happy today.

rules.body_en: An adverb tells you how something happens. It describes a verb. Most adverbs are made from an adjective + -ly: slow – slowly, quick – quickly, careful – carefully, quiet – quietly. Compare: a quiet voice (adjective) and she speaks quietly (adverb).
rules.body_ru: Наречие говорит, как происходит действие, и описывает глагол. Большинство наречий образуются от прилагательного + -ly: slow – slowly, quick – quickly, careful – carefully, quiet – quietly. Сравните: a quiet voice (прилагательное) и she speaks quietly (наречие). По-русски это разница между «тихий» и «тихо».

examples.en: He drives carefully.
Please speak slowly.
The children played quietly.

rules.body_en: Adjectives ending in -y change y to i: happy – happily, easy – easily. Adjectives ending in -le drop the e and add -y: gentle – gently, terrible – terribly. Adjectives ending in -ful add -ly with double l: careful – carefully, beautiful – beautifully.
rules.body_ru: Прилагательные на -y меняют y на i: happy – happily, easy – easily. Прилагательные на -le теряют e и получают -y: gentle – gently, terrible – terribly. Прилагательные на -ful получают -ly с двойной l: careful – carefully, beautiful – beautifully.

examples.en: She sings beautifully.
I passed the test easily.
They lived happily together.

rules.title_en: Irregular adverbs: well, fast, hard, late
rules.title_ru: Особые наречия: well, fast, hard, late
rules.body_en: The adverb of good is well: a good singer – she sings well. Some adverbs look the same as the adjective: fast – fast, hard – hard, late – late, early – early. Be careful: hardly means 'almost not' and lately means 'recently', so they are different words.
rules.body_ru: Наречие от good – well: a good singer – she sings well. Некоторые наречия совпадают с прилагательным: fast – fast, hard – hard, late – late, early – early. Осторожно: hardly значит «почти не», а lately – «в последнее время», это другие слова. Типичная ошибка: «she sings good» – неправильно.

examples.en: He speaks English well.
She works hard and drives fast.
examples.ru: Она много работает и быстро ездит.

examples.en: We got up late on Sunday.

rules.body_en: Adverbs of manner go after the verb or after the object: She speaks English well (not 'she speaks well English'). Adverbs of frequency (always, often, never) go before the main verb but after be: I always walk to work. I am never late. Time words usually go at the end or the beginning: I went there yesterday.
rules.body_ru: Наречия образа действия ставятся после глагола или после дополнения: She speaks English well (нельзя «she speaks well English»). Наречия частоты (always, often, never) стоят перед основным глаголом, но после be: I always walk to work. I am never late. Слова времени обычно в конце или в начале: I went there yesterday. В русском порядок слов свободнее, в английском его нужно соблюдать.

examples.en: He plays the piano very well.
examples.ru: Он очень хорошо играет на пианино.

examples.en: We usually have dinner at seven.
She is often tired after work.

rules.body_en: Too + adjective means 'more than is good': It's too hot. Enough goes after an adjective (big enough, old enough) but before a noun (enough money, enough time). With nouns we say too much (uncountable) or too many (countable): too much sugar, too many people.
rules.body_ru: Too + прилагательное значит «слишком»: It's too hot. Enough («достаточно») стоит после прилагательного (big enough, old enough), но перед существительным (enough money, enough time). С существительными говорят too much (неисчисляемые) или too many (исчисляемые): too much sugar, too many people. Обратите внимание на позицию enough – она отличается от русского.

examples.en: This coffee is too hot to drink.
examples.ru: Этот кофе слишком горячий, чтобы пить.

examples.en: He isn't old enough to drive.
examples.ru: Он недостаточно взрослый, чтобы водить машину.

examples.en: We don't have enough time.
There were too many people.

rules.body_en: After the verbs look, feel, sound, smell and taste we use an adjective, not an adverb, because they describe the subject: You look great. This soup smells good. It sounds interesting. Do not say 'it smells well'.
rules.body_ru: После глаголов look, feel, sound, smell и taste используется прилагательное, а не наречие, потому что они описывают подлежащее, а не действие: You look great. This soup smells good. It sounds interesting. Нельзя сказать «it smells well».

examples.en: You look tired. Are you OK?
examples.ru: Ты выглядишь уставшим. Всё в порядке?

examples.en: This cake tastes wonderful.
I feel happy today.

rules.body_en: Very, really and quite make an adjective or adverb stronger or weaker: very good, really fast, quite difficult. They go before the adjective or adverb. Quite means 'a little more than a bit, but not very': The film was quite good.
rules.body_ru: Very, really и quite усиливают или смягчают прилагательное или наречие: very good («очень»), really fast («действительно, очень»), quite difficult («довольно»). Они ставятся перед прилагательным или наречием. Quite – это «довольно, достаточно», не так сильно, как very: The film was quite good.

examples.en: She speaks really quickly.
The hotel was quite expensive.
It's a very interesting city.

exercises.q: She speaks English very ___ .
exercises.explain_en: We need an adverb to describe 'speaks'. The adverb of good is well.
exercises.explain_ru: Нужно наречие к глаголу speaks. Наречие от good – well.

exercises.q: He is a ___ driver.
exercises.explain_en: Before a noun (driver) we use an adjective.
exercises.explain_ru: Перед существительным (driver) нужно прилагательное.

exercises.q: Please drive ___ .
exercises.explain_en: An adverb describes the verb 'drive': slowly.
exercises.explain_ru: Наречие описывает глагол drive: slowly.

exercises.q: This coffee is ___ hot. I can't drink it.
exercises.explain_en: Too + adjective = more than is good.
exercises.explain_ru: Too + прилагательное = «слишком».

exercises.q: The room isn't big ___ for ten people.
exercises.explain_en: Enough goes after the adjective: big enough.
exercises.explain_ru: Enough ставится после прилагательного: big enough.

exercises.q: She always works ___ .
exercises.explain_en: The adverb of 'hard' is 'hard'. 'Hardly' means 'almost not'.
exercises.explain_ru: Наречие от hard – hard. Hardly значит «почти не».

exercises.q: They arrived ___ .
exercises.explain_en: 'Late' is both adjective and adverb. 'Lately' means 'recently'.
exercises.explain_ru: Late – и прилагательное, и наречие. Lately значит «в последнее время».

exercises.q: I ___ late for work.
exercises.explain_en: Adverbs of frequency go after 'be': I am never late.
exercises.explain_ru: Наречия частоты ставятся после be: I am never late.

exercises.q: He runs very ___ (quick).
exercises.explain_en: Adverb: quick + -ly.
exercises.explain_ru: Наречие: quick + -ly.

exercises.q: She sings ___ (good).
exercises.explain_en: The adverb of good is well.
exercises.explain_ru: Наречие от good – well.

exercises.q: The children played ___ (happy) in the garden.
exercises.explain_en: Change y to i and add -ly: happily.
exercises.explain_ru: Меняем y на i и добавляем -ly: happily.

exercises.q: This bag is ___ heavy. I can't carry it. (too / enough)
exercises.explain_en: Too heavy = so heavy that I can't carry it.
exercises.explain_ru: Too heavy = настолько тяжёлая, что не могу нести.

exercises.q: He isn't old ___ to drive. (too / enough)
exercises.explain_en: Adjective + enough: old enough.
exercises.explain_ru: Прилагательное + enough: old enough.

exercises.q: He drives very ___ (fast).
exercises.explain_en: 'Fast' is the same as adjective and adverb. There is no 'fastly'.
exercises.explain_ru: Fast одинаково как прилагательное и наречие. Слова «fastly» нет.

exercises.q: 'She speaks well English' is correct word order.
exercises.explain_en: The adverb goes after the object: She speaks English well.
exercises.explain_ru: Наречие стоит после дополнения: She speaks English well.

exercises.q: 'Hard' and 'hardly' mean the same.
exercises.explain_en: Hard = with effort; hardly = almost not.
exercises.explain_ru: Hard – усердно, тяжело; hardly – почти не.

exercises.q: 'Enough' comes after an adjective: big enough.
exercises.explain_en: Yes: big enough, good enough. But: enough money.
exercises.explain_ru: Верно: big enough, good enough. Но: enough money.

exercises.q: The adverb of 'good' is 'well'.
exercises.explain_en: Yes: a good player plays well.
exercises.explain_ru: Верно: a good player plays well.

exercises.q: 'I have too many work' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: Work is uncountable: too much work.
exercises.explain_ru: Work неисчисляемое: too much work.

exercises.answer: She speaks French very well.
He drives too fast.
The soup isn't hot enough.
They walked slowly along the beach.

sections.summary_en: Past continuous (was/were + -ing) describes an action in progress in the past. With when and while it combines with past simple: I was walking home when it started to rain.
sections.summary_ru: Past Continuous (was/were + -ing) описывает действие, которое длилось в прошлом. С when и while он сочетается с Past Simple: I was walking home when it started to rain.

rules.body_en: The past continuous is was/were + verb-ing: I was sleeping, you were working, she was reading, they were playing. Use was with I, he, she, it and were with you, we, they. The -ing spelling rules are the same as in the present continuous.
rules.body_ru: Past Continuous образуется как was/were + глагол с -ing: I was sleeping, you were working, she was reading, they were playing. Was – с I, he, she, it; were – с you, we, they. Правила написания -ing такие же, как в Present Continuous.

examples.en: I was watching TV at nine o'clock.
examples.ru: В девять часов я смотрел телевизор.

examples.en: They were waiting for the bus.
She was making dinner.

rules.title_en: An action in progress in the past
rules.body_en: Use the past continuous for an action that was happening at a certain moment in the past. The action started before that moment and continued after it: At eight o'clock I was having breakfast. This time yesterday we were flying to Rome.
rules.body_ru: Past Continuous описывает действие, которое происходило в определённый момент прошлого: оно началось раньше и продолжалось после этого момента: At eight o'clock I was having breakfast. This time yesterday we were flying to Rome. По смыслу это близко к русскому несовершенному виду: «я завтракал», «мы летели».

examples.en: What were you doing at ten last night?
examples.ru: Что ты делал вчера в десять вечера?

examples.en: At midnight everyone was still dancing.

rules.body_en: We often use the past continuous for a long background action and the past simple for a short action that interrupts it: I was walking home when it started to rain. She was sleeping when the phone rang. The short action is in the past simple.
rules.body_ru: Часто Past Continuous используется для длинного фонового действия, а Past Simple – для короткого действия, которое его прерывает: I was walking home when it started to rain («я шёл домой, когда начался дождь»). She was sleeping when the phone rang. Короткое действие всегда в Past Simple. Сравните с русским: «шёл» (длилось) и «начался» (случилось).

examples.en: I was cooking when he arrived.
We were driving home when we saw the accident.
examples.ru: Мы ехали домой, когда увидели аварию.

examples.en: He broke his leg while he was skiing.
examples.ru: Он сломал ногу, когда катался на лыжах.

rules.body_en: When usually goes with the past simple (the short action): I was reading when you called. While usually goes with the past continuous (the long action): While I was reading, you called. The clause with when/while can go first or second; if it goes first, put a comma after it.
rules.body_ru: When обычно идёт с Past Simple (короткое действие): I was reading when you called. While обычно идёт с Past Continuous (длинное действие): While I was reading, you called. Часть с when/while может стоять в начале или в конце; если в начале – после неё ставится запятая. While по-русски – «пока, в то время как».

examples.en: While she was working, the children were sleeping.
The lights went off while we were eating.
When I saw him, he was running.
examples.ru: Когда я его увидел, он бежал.

rules.title_en: Two long actions at the same time
rules.body_en: When two actions were happening at the same time, use the past continuous for both, often with while: While I was cooking, my brother was watching TV. They were talking and laughing all evening.
rules.body_ru: Если два действия происходили одновременно, оба ставятся в Past Continuous, обычно с while: While I was cooking, my brother was watching TV. They were talking and laughing all evening. По-русски: «пока я готовил, брат смотрел телевизор».

examples.en: While I was studying, my friends were playing football.
examples.ru: Пока я занимался, мои друзья играли в футбол.

examples.en: She was reading and he was listening to music.
examples.ru: Она читала, а он слушал музыку.

rules.body_en: Questions: put was/were before the subject: Was she working? Were you sleeping? What were you doing? Short answers: Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't. Negatives: wasn't / weren't + verb-ing: He wasn't listening. They weren't playing.
rules.body_ru: Вопросы: was/were ставится перед подлежащим: Was she working? Were you sleeping? What were you doing? Краткие ответы: Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't. Отрицания: wasn't / weren't + глагол с -ing: He wasn't listening. They weren't playing.

examples.en: Were you listening to me? – Yes, I was.
Was it raining when you left?
I wasn't sleeping, I was reading.

rules.body_en: As in the present, state verbs (know, like, want, understand, believe, have = own) are not used in the continuous form. Say I knew the answer, not 'I was knowing'. She wanted to go, not 'she was wanting'.
rules.body_ru: Как и в настоящем времени, глаголы состояния (know, like, want, understand, believe, have = владеть) не используются в Continuous. Говорите I knew the answer, а не «I was knowing». She wanted to go, а не «she was wanting». Даже если по-русски действие «длилось» (я знал, хотел), в английском нужен Past Simple.

examples.en: I knew him when he was a child.
examples.ru: Я знал его, когда он был ребёнком.

examples.en: We wanted to leave, but it was raining.
examples.ru: Мы хотели уйти, но шёл дождь.

rules.title_en: Setting the scene in a story
rules.body_en: At the start of a story, the past continuous describes the situation and the weather, and the past simple tells what happened: The sun was shining and the birds were singing. Suddenly, I heard a noise.
rules.body_ru: В начале рассказа Past Continuous описывает обстановку и погоду, а Past Simple – то, что случилось: The sun was shining and the birds were singing. Suddenly, I heard a noise. Это удобный способ «нарисовать фон» перед главным событием.

examples.en: It was raining and people were running to the bus.
examples.ru: Шёл дождь, и люди бежали к автобусу.

examples.en: The children were playing in the park when it happened.
examples.ru: Дети играли в парке, когда это случилось.

exercises.q: At nine o'clock last night I ___ TV when the phone rang.
exercises.explain_en: A long action in progress: was watching.
exercises.explain_ru: Длительное действие в процессе: was watching.

exercises.q: They ___ football when it started to rain.
exercises.explain_en: With 'they' use were + -ing.
exercises.explain_ru: С they – were + -ing.

exercises.q: I was walking home ___ I saw Tom.
exercises.explain_en: The short action (saw) goes with 'when'.
exercises.explain_ru: Короткое действие (saw) вводится словом when.

exercises.q: ___ she was cooking, the children were playing.
exercises.explain_en: Two long actions at the same time: while.
exercises.explain_ru: Два долгих действия одновременно: while.

exercises.q: ___ you ___ at ten o'clock yesterday?
exercises.explain_en: Question: Were + you + working.
exercises.explain_ru: Вопрос: Were + you + working.

exercises.q: We ___ the answer.
exercises.explain_en: 'Know' is a state verb: no continuous form.
exercises.explain_ru: Know – глагол состояния: без Continuous.

exercises.q: He ___ when I called.
exercises.explain_en: Negative: wasn't + -ing with 'he'.
exercises.explain_ru: Отрицание: wasn't + -ing с he.

exercises.q: The sun ___ and the birds ___ .
exercises.explain_en: The sun (it) takes was; the birds (they) take were.
exercises.explain_ru: The sun (это it) – was; the birds (это they) – were.

exercises.q: I ___ (read) when you called.
exercises.explain_en: Long action: was reading.
exercises.explain_ru: Длительное действие: was reading.

exercises.q: They ___ (not / sleep) at midnight.
exercises.explain_en: Negative with they: weren't sleeping.
exercises.explain_ru: Отрицание с they: weren't sleeping.

exercises.q: ___ (it / rain) when you left?
exercises.explain_en: Question: Was + it + raining.
exercises.explain_ru: Вопрос: Was + it + raining.

exercises.q: While she ___ (drive) to work, she saw the accident.
exercises.explain_en: After 'while' use the past continuous.
exercises.explain_ru: После while используется Past Continuous.

exercises.q: I ___ (break) my leg while I was skiing.
exercises.explain_en: The short action is in the past simple: broke.
exercises.explain_ru: Короткое действие – в Past Simple: broke.

exercises.q: What ___ (you / do) at eight last night?
exercises.explain_en: Question word + were + subject + -ing.
exercises.explain_ru: Вопросительное слово + were + подлежащее + -ing.

exercises.q: The past continuous is formed with was/were + verb-ing.
exercises.explain_en: Yes: I was reading, they were playing.
exercises.explain_ru: Верно: I was reading, they were playing.

exercises.q: 'I was knowing him' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: 'Know' is a state verb: I knew him.
exercises.explain_ru: Know – глагол состояния: I knew him.

exercises.q: 'While' is usually followed by the past continuous.
exercises.explain_en: Yes: While I was cooking, ...
exercises.explain_ru: Верно: While I was cooking, ...

exercises.q: 'When the phone rang, I was having a shower' is correct.
exercises.explain_en: Short action (rang) + long action (was having).
exercises.explain_ru: Короткое действие (rang) + длительное (was having).

exercises.q: 'They was watching TV' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: With they use were: They were watching TV.
exercises.explain_ru: С they нужно were: They were watching TV.

exercises.answer: I was sleeping when you called.
What were you doing at six?
While we were walking, it started to rain.
She wasn't listening to the teacher.

sections.title_en: Prepositions, phrasal verbs and word order
sections.title_ru: Предлоги, фразовые глаголы и порядок слов
sections.summary_en: Prepositions of movement (into, across, through), verbs with prepositions (listen to, wait for), basic phrasal verbs (turn off, look for) and where the object goes.
sections.summary_ru: Предлоги движения (into, across, through), глаголы с предлогами (listen to, wait for), базовые фразовые глаголы (turn off, look for) и место дополнения в предложении.

rules.body_en: Movement words answer 'where to?': to (a place), into (inside), out of, across (from one side to the other), along (following a line), through (inside, from one end to the other), over, under, up, down, past, towards, from. We say go to school, walk into the room, run across the road.
rules.body_ru: Предлоги движения отвечают на вопрос «куда?»: to (к месту), into (внутрь), out of (из), across (через, с одной стороны на другую), along (вдоль), through (сквозь, насквозь), over (через, поверх), under, up, down, past (мимо), towards (по направлению к), from. Говорят go to school, walk into the room, run across the road. Русское «в» – это to (к месту) или into (внутрь), а не in.

examples.en: She walked into the shop.
We drove through the tunnel.
He ran across the road.
Go along this street and turn left.
examples.ru: Идите вдоль этой улицы и поверните налево.

rules.title_ru: Home, here и there: без to
rules.body_en: After go, come, get and arrive we do not use 'to' before home, here and there: go home, come here, get there. But we do use 'to' with other places: go to work, come to my house. Arrive uses at or in, never to: arrive at the station, arrive in London.
rules.body_ru: После go, come, get и arrive перед home, here и there предлог to не ставится: go home, come here, get there. С другими местами to нужен: go to work, come to my house. Arrive сочетается с at или in, но никогда с to: arrive at the station, arrive in London. Типичная ошибка: «go to home».

examples.en: I usually go home at six.
examples.ru: Обычно я иду домой в шесть.

examples.en: Come here, please.
We arrived at the airport at ten.
examples.ru: Мы прибыли в аэропорт в десять.

rules.body_en: Some verbs always need a preposition before the object: listen to music, look at a picture, wait for a bus, talk to a friend, think about a problem, depend on the weather, ask for help. These are often different from Russian, so learn the verb and the preposition together.
rules.body_ru: Некоторые глаголы всегда требуют предлог перед дополнением: listen to music, look at a picture, wait for a bus, talk to a friend, think about a problem, depend on the weather, ask for help. Предлоги часто не совпадают с русскими («слушать музыку» – без предлога, а listen to music – с предлогом), поэтому учите глагол вместе с предлогом.

examples.en: Listen to me!
I'm waiting for my friend.
It depends on the price.

rules.body_en: A phrasal verb is a verb plus a small word (up, off, on, out) that together have a new meaning: get up (leave your bed), turn off (stop a machine), put on (dress), take off (undress), look for (search), give up (stop doing), find out (learn information), pick up (take in your hand).
rules.body_ru: Фразовый глагол – это глагол плюс маленькое слово (up, off, on, out), которые вместе получают новое значение: get up (вставать), turn off (выключать), put on (надевать), take off (снимать), look for (искать), give up (бросать), find out (узнавать), pick up (поднимать, брать). Значение часто нельзя угадать по частям, поэтому их учат как одно слово.

examples.en: I get up at seven every day.
examples.ru: Я встаю в семь каждый день.

examples.en: Put on your coat, it's cold.
I'm looking for my glasses.

rules.title_en: Separable phrasal verbs: where the object goes
rules.body_en: With many phrasal verbs (turn off, put on, pick up, take off), a noun object can go after the particle or between the verb and the particle: turn off the light / turn the light off. But a pronoun (it, them, him) must go in the middle: turn it off, never 'turn off it'.
rules.body_ru: У многих фразовых глаголов (turn off, put on, pick up, take off) существительное-дополнение может стоять после частицы или между глаголом и частицей: turn off the light / turn the light off. Но местоимение (it, them, him) обязательно ставится в середину: turn it off, и никогда «turn off it».

examples.en: Turn the TV off. / Turn off the TV.
Turn it off, please.
Pick them up and put them away.

rules.body_en: Some phrasal verbs cannot be separated; the object always comes after the particle: look for, look after (take care of), get on / get off (a bus), look at, listen to. Say I'm looking for it, not 'I'm looking it for'.
rules.body_ru: Некоторые фразовые глаголы не разделяются: дополнение всегда идёт после частицы: look for (искать), look after (заботиться), get on / get off (садиться в транспорт / выходить), look at, listen to. Говорите I'm looking for it, а не «I'm looking it for».

examples.en: She looks after her little brother.
Get off the bus at the next stop.
examples.ru: Выходи из автобуса на следующей остановке.

examples.en: I'm looking for them everywhere.

rules.title_en: Basic word order: subject, verb, object
rules.title_ru: Базовый порядок слов: подлежащее, глагол, дополнение
rules.body_en: English word order is fixed: subject + verb + object: I like coffee. Then place, then time: I played tennis in the park yesterday. Do not put a word between the verb and its object: I like coffee very much, not 'I like very much coffee'.
rules.body_ru: В английском порядок слов фиксированный: подлежащее + глагол + дополнение: I like coffee. Затем место, затем время: I played tennis in the park yesterday. Между глаголом и дополнением ничего не ставится: I like coffee very much, а не «I like very much coffee». В русском порядок свободный («Кофе я люблю»), в английском так нельзя.

examples.en: We watched a film at home last night.
examples.ru: Вчера вечером мы смотрели фильм дома.

examples.en: She speaks English very well.
I met Tom in London last year.
examples.ru: Я встретил Тома в Лондоне в прошлом году.

rules.title_en: Prepositions at the end of questions
rules.body_en: When a verb has a preposition, the preposition usually goes at the end of the question: Who are you waiting for? What are you looking at? Where do you come from? Do not start the question with the preposition in everyday English.
rules.body_ru: Если у глагола есть предлог, в вопросе он обычно уходит в конец: Who are you waiting for? What are you looking at? Where do you come from? В разговорном английском вопрос не начинают с предлога. По-русски предлог стоит в начале («Кого ты ждёшь?» – «За кем?»), поэтому эта структура кажется непривычной.

examples.en: Who are you talking to?
What are you thinking about?
Where are you from?

exercises.q: She walked ___ the room and sat down.
exercises.explain_en: Movement to the inside: into.
exercises.explain_ru: Движение внутрь: into.

exercises.q: Can you turn ___ the TV? I want to watch the news.
exercises.explain_en: Turn on = start a machine.
exercises.explain_ru: Turn on = включить.

exercises.q: I'm looking ___ my keys. Have you seen them?
exercises.explain_en: Look for = search.
exercises.explain_ru: Look for = искать.

exercises.q: The music is too loud. Please turn ___ .
exercises.explain_en: A pronoun goes between the verb and the particle: turn it off.
exercises.explain_ru: Местоимение ставится между глаголом и частицей: turn it off.

exercises.q: We drove ___ the tunnel.
exercises.explain_en: Through = inside, from one end to the other.
exercises.explain_ru: Through = сквозь, от одного конца до другого.

exercises.q: After work I usually go ___ .
exercises.explain_en: No 'to' before home: go home.
exercises.explain_ru: Перед home предлог to не нужен: go home.

exercises.q: Who are you waiting ___ ?
exercises.explain_en: Wait for someone. The preposition goes at the end.
exercises.explain_ru: Wait for = ждать кого-то. Предлог в конце вопроса.

exercises.q: I ___ every day.
exercises.explain_en: Verb + object + place + time.
exercises.explain_ru: Глагол + дополнение + место + время.

exercises.q: Listen ___ me! (preposition)
exercises.explain_en: Listen always takes 'to'.
exercises.explain_ru: Listen всегда с предлогом to.

exercises.q: The bus is coming. Let's get ___ . (on / off)
exercises.explain_en: Get on = enter a bus or train.
exercises.explain_ru: Get on = сесть в автобус или поезд.

exercises.q: It's cold. Put ___ your coat. (on / off)
exercises.explain_en: Put on = dress; take off = undress.
exercises.explain_ru: Put on = надеть; take off = снять.

exercises.q: The phone is ringing. Please pick ___ . (it up / up it)
exercises.explain_en: A pronoun goes in the middle: pick it up.
exercises.explain_ru: Местоимение ставится в середину: pick it up.

exercises.q: I'll look ___ your cat while you're away. (after / for)
exercises.explain_en: Look after = take care of.
exercises.explain_ru: Look after = присматривать, заботиться.

exercises.q: He ran ___ the road to the other side. (across / along)
exercises.explain_en: Across = from one side to the other.
exercises.explain_ru: Across = с одной стороны на другую.

exercises.q: 'Turn off it' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: A pronoun must go in the middle: turn it off.
exercises.explain_ru: Местоимение должно стоять в середине: turn it off.

exercises.q: 'I went to home' is correct English.
exercises.explain_en: No 'to' before home: I went home.
exercises.explain_ru: Перед home нет to: I went home.

exercises.q: In 'look for', the object cannot go between 'look' and 'for'.
exercises.explain_en: Look for is inseparable: look for it.
exercises.explain_ru: Look for не разделяется: look for it.

exercises.q: 'Through' means from one side of something to the other, inside it.
exercises.explain_en: Yes: through the tunnel, through the forest.
exercises.explain_ru: Верно: through the tunnel, through the forest.

exercises.q: 'I like very much coffee' is correct word order.
exercises.explain_en: The object comes right after the verb: I like coffee very much.
exercises.explain_ru: Дополнение идёт сразу после глагола: I like coffee very much.

exercises.answer: Please turn the music down.
She gets up at seven every day.
exercises.ru: Она встаёт в семь каждый день.

exercises.answer: What are you looking at?
We walked along the river to the bridge.
exercises.ru: Мы шли вдоль реки до моста.
